outputs.description: Density-threshold vs disk size-mass confound test on SPARC
outputs.method: R_DM = first radius with Vobs/Vbar > threshold (step_4 convention), evaluated both on all discrete grid crossings and on bracketed log-interpolated interior crossings (excluding left-censored idx == 0 galaxies where Vobs/Vbar > threshold already at the innermost beam/sampling radius R_min).

tobit_left_censored_size_invariant_test.note: Low-surface-brightness dwarfs with central Sigma_0 < Sigma_crit are unscreened to r=0 (R_DM = 0 physically); treating R_DM = 0 systems as finite log-normal upper bounds log10(R_DM) <= log10(R_min) pulls the low-mass tail toward -inf and inflates the apparent log-log slope above the resolved interior crossing slope (0.36-0.49) and the Step 12 two-branch kinetic law (0.502).

Low-surface-brightness dwarfs with central Sigma_0 < Sigma_crit are unscreened to r=0 (R_DM = 0 physically); treating R_DM = 0 systems as finite log-normal upper bounds log10(R_DM) <= log10(R_min) pulls the low-mass tail toward -inf and inflates the apparent log-log slope above the resolved interior crossing slope (0.36-0.49) and the Step 12 two-branch kinetic law (0.502).

Low-surface-brightness dwarfs with central Sigma_0 < Sigma_crit are unscreened to r=0 (R_DM = 0 physically); treating R_DM = 0 systems as finite log-normal upper bounds log10(R_DM) <= log10(R_min) pulls the low-mass tail toward -inf and inflates the apparent log-log slope above the resolved interior crossing slope (0.36-0.49) and the Step 12 two-branch kinetic law (0.502).

outputs.description: Phantom-mass amplitude and radial-profile test on SPARC
outputs.method: Plateau ratio = median V_obs/V_bar over outer third of each curve (signed V_gas convention). Linear-kinetic baseline S_eff = (ratio^2 - 1)/(2 beta_A^2) with |beta_A| = 1 (ceiling sqrt(3) = 1.732), evaluated alongside the selected two-branch kinetic completion P_X = eps_reg + k sqrt(xi) + 2 xi (k = 16.03, zero free parameters). Enhancement profile slope = d log E / d log R with E = V_obs^2/V_bar^2 - 1 = M_ph/M_bar(<R). V_bar floor 5.0 km/s, >= 6 valid points required.

rar_prediction.primary_force_law: g_obs = g_N + a_phi (action-derived additive force law from L_pp = -mc sqrt(-g_tilde_munu dx^mu dx^nu))
rar_prediction.calibration_provenance: k_star = 4 sqrt(2) g_t / a_0 = 16.03 calibrated to empirical scale a_0 = 1.2e-10 m/s^2 (not an independent prediction of a_0)

quality_controlled_sparc_sample.selection_cuts: Q <= 2, i >= 30 deg, e_Vobs / V_obs <= 0.10 (Lelli et al. 2017 standard SPARC RAR cuts)

k_scan.note: Under the action-derived additive force law g_obs = g_N + a_phi (with zero-gradient regulator eps_reg = 1e-3), the calibrated k_star = 16.03 gives RMS = 0.2185 dex at Upsilon_d = 0.5 and 0.2004 dex at Upsilon_d = 0.35 (improving over the 0.2812 dex unit-term baseline and 0.2749 dex exp-interp rival by >60 mdex); the empirical quadrature comparator sqrt(g_N^2 + a_phi^2) (0.1974 dex) is recorded separately as a phenomenological interpolating reference rather than an action-derived force law.

btfr.note: V_flat^4 = G M_b a_eff with a_eff = 4 sqrt(2) g_t/k; M_b = Ups_d L3.6 + 1.33 M_HI. Full per-galaxy BTFR analysis is performed in step_13_two_branch_btfr.py.

transition_shape_scan.family: P_X = k sqrt(xi) + 2 xi + c2 xi^{3/2}
transition_shape_scan.note: subleading xi^{3/2} term preserves both asymptotic branches; reported as a diagnostic of what mid-range suppression the SPARC distribution requires, not as a fitted sector

transition_qcoef_scan.note: the xi coefficient controls suppression in the SPARC window (xi ~ 0.01-1); scanned to quantify the mid-range deformation the data would require if the offset were sector-internal

ambient_field_scan.note: positive u_amb raises the predicted curve; since the transition residual is already negative (obs below pred), the scan bounds the ambient shear allowed by SPARC

upsilon_disk_scan.note: disk M/L rescales g_bar horizontally; reported to quantify how much of the transition offset is absorbed by the canonical M/L uncertainty rather than the sector shape

unit_term_scan.note: eps <= 0.1 is observationally free and slightly improves the fit; eps ~ 0.3 reaches the MOND-reference rms but restores a linear (Keplerian) tail below g_N ~ (eps/k) g_t, conflicting with the flat-asymptote requirement that selects p=1/2.  The admissible regulator window is therefore small-eps (fixes the X->0 degeneracy at zero data cost), consistent with the step_62 growth scan where even eps = 1 shifts chi2 by < 0.1.

outputs.model: J_i = K(psi) f(q) a_i, K = e^{c psi}, psi = inward-integrated pair-well depth per galaxy
outputs.note: c=0 recovers step_10 two-branch pointwise result up to the radial integration convention

inner_peak_mass_proxy_diagnostic.note: Evaluating R*V_bar^2/G at argmax(V_bar^2) instead of R_max underestimates M_bar in bulge/compact spirals and flattens the apparent slope to 0.272; using R_max recovers slope = 0.5022, matching the two-branch prediction 0.500 to 0.4%.

zero_parameter.note: The -0.173 dex intercept offset relative to sqrt(G M_bar(R_max)/a_eff) reflects the enclosed baryonic mass fraction f_enc = M_bar(<r_on)/M_bar(R_max) ~= 0.65 at the interior crossing radius r_on.

asymptotic.note: deep-limit formula underpredicts v_flat at finite u (g_N/g_t ~ 0.02 at outer radii), where the two-branch finite-radius slope is 3.53-3.64 and inverse-OLS on the quality-filtered sample recovers 3.76-3.86; the outer-edge test is the direct finite-u comparison

amplitude_law_check.statement: S_A = min[1,(rho/rho_T)^(1/3)] is exactly u_min(rho)/u_min(rho_T) for the quartic branch: the corpus response exponent 1/3 = 1/(m-1) fixes m = 4.

self_quenching_crossing.statement: under the corpus normalization the u ~ 1 crossing sits at ~1e26 g/cm^3 (temporal-well interior), not at rho_T = 20 g/cm^3.

failures: u_min(NS core) ~ 21 > u_s = 10: pulsars would sit on the Planck-density floor (temporal wells), excluded
lambda_c(rho_T) >> any body radius: the invoked local equilibrium never forms; mechanism inert where claimed

kinetic_column_scale.statement: the X|X|/Lambda_X^4 interior turns canonical below surface density ~ 0.1 g/cm^2 (~ 570 M_sun/pc^2): the kinetic scale supplies a column-density floor, not a volume-density scale.

prem_earth_bvp_integration.model: 4-layer PREM spherical Earth BVP solve of nabla^2 u = M_Pl^-2 V_eff'(u) with 3D Yukawa-propagated datum-free surface covariance projection

full_volume_yukawa_integral.note: Integrating across all interior shells r in [500, 6321] km weighted by r^2|du/dr| yields L_c = 3044-3213 km (R^2 = 0.981-0.985), matching the 25.3-yr isotropic CODE baseline (3210 +- 389 km, Paper 2) and ESA Final (3193 km), while the transition-centroid shell (R_grad = 4875 km) yields L_c = 4010 km matching the cross-sector/PPP baseline (4201 km).

correlated_orbital_datum_null_gps_only.injected_signal: Rank-3 satellite-orbit/geocenter dipole cos(d/R_E) + reference-clock datum common mode (zero TEP exponential)
correlated_orbital_datum_null_gps_only.verdict: Concave-down dipole curvature (d2C/dd2 < 0 vs > 0 for exponential) drives unconstrained exponential fit to upper bound (~24,900 km); GPS-only processing does not manufacture a 4,200 km scale from correlated orbital/datum errors.

isb_parameterization_sensitivity.note: Per-epoch ISB projection yields 2,277 +- 47 km (1.77x compression, matching CNES/GRG 1,933 km), whereas daily-constant ISB with rotating constellation visibility yields 2,482 +- 46 km (1.63x compression, matching CODE matched-day MGEX 2,744 km). Both spatial ISB projection and wavenumber passband filtering describe the same removal of l=0,1 long-wavelength spherical-harmonic modes.

constellation_debiasing_synthesis.statement: Forward Monte Carlo injection of a single L_c = 4200 km station-clock correlation field into a 120-station global network shows that 1-constellation GPS-only global datum removal recovers L_c = 4036 +- 113 km (R^2 = 0.999, bias -3.9%; white-noise null returns |C(d)| = 0.009 +- 0.001 with no spurious scale), whereas 4-constellation multi-GNSS common-view ISB projection compresses the same injected field to L_c = 2277 +- 47 km (derived compression ratio 1.77 +- 0.06, matching the empirical 4066 / 2141 = 1.90x ratio).

mars_unmodeled_transition_body.note: Low-mass Mars (0.11 M_earth) sits in the transition region between the ambient curve (0.099 km/s) and the small-body soliton capacity curve (0.768 km/s) without a Mars-specific rule.

bryan_2020_pmo_breakup_envelope_test.falsifier: Any unbraked planetary-mass companion or brown dwarf with M > M_cap = 0.61 M_Jup and v_eq / v_breakup > 0.45 falsifies the soliton angular-momentum capacity bound.
